cefrAlignment: Matches the B2 written production descriptor (an essay that develops an argument, giving reasons for or against a point of view, with relevant supporting detail); the models are clear, well-organised B2+/band 7-ish prose without exceeding learner reach.
examFidelity: IELTS Task 2 (250+ words, about 40 minutes, Task 2 counting twice as much as Task 1) and TOEIC opinion essay (30 minutes, ETS: an effective essay typically has at least 300 words) now match exams.ts and the official ETS/ielts.org wording.
fixes: Removed the unverified claim that 'many candidates do Task 2 first'; the tip now states the verified weighting (Task 2 contributes twice as much) and advises not letting Task 1 overrun
TOEIC 300-word figure reworded in the MCQ explanation and exam tip to ETS's own framing ('an effective essay typically has at least 300 words'), verified against the ETS sample-test directions
Labelled the TOEIC example instruction as 'typical of' the TOEIC essay instead of presenting it as the exact wording
Paragraph-length table corrected: the old ranges (40–50 + 80–90 + 80–90 + 30–40) added up to only 230–270 words, below the 250-word minimum; now about 90–100 words per body paragraph
Model essay: reworded the ambiguous 'a small price to pay for students who are more caring' and updated the stated length (about 280 words)

Practice model answer: added a concrete example to body paragraph 2 so it models the lesson's topic sentence, explanation, example and link pattern; fixed 'decisions about their health, money or votes'
openConcerns: Writing tasks are self-assessed against the rubric; a teacher or a scoring tool would be needed for reliable band feedback
learnerOutcome: A learner can plan and write a consistent four-paragraph opinion essay with a clear thesis and developed body paragraphs, at the right length for IELTS Task 2 or the TOEIC opinion essay.
